fix: Read the list through the borrowing accessor instead of cloning the whole Vec<DocumentTab> each build: `state.editor.documents.with(|documents| { ... })` around the body that uses `documents` (the tab loop and `documents.get(active_idx)`). Every closure only needs the signal clones already taken on lines 25-26, so nothing else changes.

`TextEditingController::text()` returns an owned String (crates/incular-text/src/editing.rs:415), so this clones the whole buffer just to count lines. Add a borrowing line-count or `with_text` accessor on the controller and use it here. Then build the gutter in one buffer: `let mut line_numbers = String::with_capacity(line_count * 4); for n in 1..=line_count { if n > 1 { line_numbers.push('\n'); } write!(line_numbers, "{n}").expect("writing to String cannot fail"); }` (with `use std::fmt::Write as _;`). This removes one String per line.
`let mut tab_widgets: Vec<Widget> = Vec::with_capacity(documents.len() + 1);` (one tab per document plus the New File button).

`text()` returns an owned copy of the whole buffer (crates/incular-text/src/editing.rs:415) and the result is only read. Take the three counts from a borrowed view instead, e.g. a `with_text(|t| (t.lines().count(), t.chars().count(), t.len()))` accessor added to TextEditingController, so the buffer is not cloned per build.

Allocates a lowercase copy of every node name on every build while a filter is active, and the loop visits all nodes. Store a pre-lowercased name on `TreeNode` when the tree is built (for example `name_lower: String`) and test `node.name_lower.contains(&filter)`. Alternatively, reuse one scratch String across nodes with `clear()` and `push_str`, but the stored field avoids the work entirely.
